_provenance.note: Wyoming dated facts. Because Wyoming has NO existing packages/snap-rules StatePolicy entry, there is no engine constant to cross-check against — every entry below is either a routine COLA-cycle reminder, a disclosed research gap, a genuinely time-sensitive not-yet-effective change, or a warning about an internal DFS-site inconsistency this pack found and resolved by treating the more clearly current source as authoritative.

entries.warning: DFS's own 'SNAP: Do I Qualify?' consumer page states a Standard Deduction of $177 (AU sizes 1-3), $184 (AU 4), $215 (AU 5), $246 (AU 6+), and a $569 maximum excess-shelter deduction — all of which are LOWER than, and do not match, the figures on DFS's own current Table I page for the same FFY2026 cycle ($209/$223/$261/$299 standard deduction, $744 shelter cap). This pack could not date-stamp the 'Do I Qualify' page's figures to a specific prior FFY cycle with certainty, but treats them as stale relative to Table I's explicitly-dated current figures. Re-verify directly with DFS, or check whether the 'Do I Qualify' page has since been updated, before citing its specific dollar figures.

Wyoming has an APPROVED but NOT-YET-EFFECTIVE federal demonstration-project waiver (approval letter dated 3/4/2026) to exclude 'sweetened, carbonated beverages' from SNAP-purchasable items statewide, effective February 1, 2027 for a 2-year period. As of this pack's fetch date (2026-08-12), SNAP recipients in Wyoming can still purchase sweetened, carbonated beverages with EBT — do not state the restriction as currently in effect until on or after 2/1/2027. Re-verify this has actually taken effect (and has not been delayed, rescinded, or modified) directly against dfs.wyo.gov or a current FNA source before that date.

This pack's conclusion that Wyoming currently has no active area-wide ABAWD waiver rests on Wyoming's complete absence from USDA FNA's SNAP Time Limit (ABAWD) Waivers FY2025-2029 state-response index as of this pack's fetch (2026-08-12), and no DFS manual section describing one. Re-check https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/waivers/timelimit/2025-2029 directly before restating this with full confidence beyond this window, since Wyoming could submit and receive a new waiver request at any time.

This pack's finding that Wyoming has fully opted out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban rests on USDA FNA's own 16th-edition State Options Report (Wyoming listed under 'No disqualification') and the DFS manual's own silence on any drug-felony disqualification section — this pack did NOT independently locate the specific Wyoming Statutes citation or DFS policy-letter authorizing this opt-out (unlike Delaware's traceable 21 DE Reg. 722 repeal order). The conclusion is well-corroborated across two independent primary sources but the underlying enabling-statute citation itself remains an unresolved, disclosed gap rather than a fabricated citation.

Wyoming's Standard Utility Allowance ($510), utilities-only standard ($340), and telephone-only allowance ($57) are drawn directly from DFS's own current, explicitly-dated Table I page — a genuine contrast with this roster's Delaware pack, which could not locate its own state's COLA notice at all. This pack did NOT separately cross-check Wyoming's specific SUA dollar figure against USDA's FY2026 national SUA self-adjustment methodology memo the way the Delaware pack attempted (and failed) to do; Wyoming's own directly-published figure is treated as authoritative and current for the FFY2026 cycle without that additional cross-check.

This pack's confirmed income-eligibility dollar figures (165%/130%/100% FPL table by household size, standard/medical/shelter/utility deductions, maximum allotments) are drawn from Wyoming DFS's current Table I page, explicitly published for the period October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026 (the FFY2026 cycle). The FFY2027 COLA cycle begins October 1, 2026 — under two months from this pack's fetch date. Check https://dfs.wyo.gov/about/policy-manuals/snap-and-power-policy-manual/table-i-snap-income-limits/ after that date before restating any Wyoming-specific income, deduction, or benefit-amount figure with full confidence; DFS's own page pattern (posting the new FFY table above the prior FFY table on the same URL) suggests the FFY2027 table should appear at the same URL when published.

This pack found USDA's Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) now redirects (HTTP 301) to a rebranded 'Food and Nutrition Administration' (FNA) domain (fna.usda.gov) for at least the SNAP State Options Report host and the ABAWD Time Limit Waivers index — a rename this pack had not previously encountered elsewhere in this roster. This pack did not independently research the scope, date, or permanence of this rebrand beyond observing the redirect; treat 'FNS' and 'FNA' as referring to the same federal agency for Wyoming SNAP administration purposes as of this pack's fetch date, but re-verify if citing the agency name directly in a context where precision matters.
